questions.q: What does Deep Packet Inspection examine that flow analysis (NetFlow) does not?
options: The actual payload content of packets, not just header metadata
The source IP address only
Nothing — DPI and flow analysis examine identical data
The physical cable the traffic travels over
questions.explain: DPI inspects application-layer payload content, while flow analysis only ever sees metadata like IPs, ports, and counters.

questions.q: Why isn't DPI typically run on every link across a large network?
options: Flow data makes DPI completely unnecessary everywhere
DPI can only process encrypted traffic, not plaintext
Buffering, reassembling, and examining payload content is resource-intensive, making full DPI impractical at full line rate everywhere
DPI hardware is illegal to deploy outside a data center
questions.explain: DPI's thoroughness comes at a real resource cost, so it's deployed at specific chokepoints rather than every link.

questions.q: In the complementary model described in this lesson, what role does flow analysis play?
options: A way to automatically block all outbound traffic
A replacement for DPI that makes DPI unnecessary
A tool that only works on encrypted traffic
Broad, always-on visibility across the network that flags where to look more closely
questions.explain: Flow analysis tells you where to look; DPI tells you what's actually there once you're looking.

questions.q: Where does DPI capability typically get deployed, and why?
options: At specific chokepoints like a perimeter firewall, because running full DPI at every link isn't practical
Nowhere — DPI is a purely theoretical concept
Only on end-user workstations
On every router and switch in the network, with no exceptions
questions.explain: Chokepoints like a perimeter firewall are where DPI's resource cost is manageable, unlike running it on every link.

questions.q: A flow record shows a host sending 80 KB to an unfamiliar external IP. Why would an analyst use DPI next, instead of running DPI on all traffic constantly?
options: DPI is resource-intensive, so it's applied selectively to traffic flow data has already flagged as worth a closer look
DPI only works on traffic under 100 KB
DPI cannot be used on any traffic flagged by NetFlow
Flow data already shows the full payload, making DPI redundant
questions.explain: This is the breadth-then-depth model: flow data narrows down where to look, and DPI is reserved for that targeted investigation.
